quotes.text: Card payments and wallet payment methods, such as Apple Pay and Google Pay, aren’t currently supported.
Payment method rules don’t apply to the [hosted invoice page]
Rules you set in your template config are inherited by all connected accounts. Connected accounts can’t override these rules.
Rules you set in your direct payment methods settings apply to destination charges. Your connected accounts’ rules don’t affect destination charges.

old_evidence.text: The configured payment method now has a **Customized** tag.
Stripe automatically calculates the equivalent limits using the current exchange rate.

findings: Both dates document merchant-set amount/country/currency visibility rules for dynamic payment methods in Payment Element, Express Checkout Element, Checkout and Payment Links. Merchant selects Customize availability and Apply Overrides on the supported method, and Stripe converts a configured limit from one currency at the current rate when evaluating a different presentment currency. A/B testing remains compatible. Availability targeting and test display are separate from an actual payment result.

November explicitly limits rules to non-card payment methods and excludes wallets including Apple Pay and Google Pay. Hosted Invoice Page is excluded in addition to the retained exclusion when the listed integrations create a subscription. The May general product language is broader; it does not prove cards, wallets or Hosted Invoice Page ever worked.

November breaks out Connect by charge type: platform template rules are inherited and cannot be overridden by a connected account for direct charges. Platform's own direct payment-method settings govern destination charges, irrespective of the connected account’s rules. The general template instruction is qualified by the named charge type. The page does not cover separate charges and transfers.

Test Checkout with `customer_email` or a Customer carrying the `+location_XX` suffix using a valid two-letter ISO country code, and Payment Links with prefilled_email or locked_prefilled_email. The URL illustrates eligible method display for a simulated country, and test cards work as usual. Node-to-cURL leaves this behavior intact.

May mentions the Customized tag and names the specific Checkout, Payment Element and Express Checkout Element sessions that meet targeting criteria; November retains Apply Overrides and also retains Payment Links prerequisites and testing, but omits that tag and result sentence. Preserve as dated rather than inferring a tag or integration removal.
Illustrative Affirm and iDEAL examples, the retargeted Connect link and Dashboard URL, and screenshot hosting/layout changes leave the underlying documented rules and test behavior unchanged.
substantive_changes: Make the explicit November non-card and wallet eligibility boundary, Hosted Invoice Page exclusion, and Connect charge-type-specific ownership and inheritance visible.
historical_claims_to_preserve: May 8 applies the named subscription-creation caveat, dynamic payment methods prerequisite, currency auto-conversion, Dashboard workflow including the then-documented Customized tag, compatible A/B testing and test market simulation. November retains the rules while sharpening scope and charge-type context.
conflicts: Current summary lines 13–21 and concept lines 10–23 omit the November card and wallet exclusions, Hosted Invoice Page and Connect direct/destination ownership.
Concept line 23 describes the Customized tag without dating it. November omits the tag text, which provides no verification of the present UI state.
The introductory Connect template instruction cannot be generalized to destination charges, which November expressly assigns to the platform’s direct configuration.
unresolved_questions: The capture does not state when the November exclusions started, establish separate-charges-and-transfers behavior or prove a live account will display a method, process a payment or outperform alternatives.
November does not verify the Customized tag persists or was removed and does not verify any linked setup details beyond the captured text.

findings: Add explicit November non-card/non-wallet scope, Hosted Invoice Page exclusion, and the Connect charge-type distinction. Preserve rule prerequisites, test behavior, A/B compatibility, currency conversion and the historic May Customized tag with dates.
conflicts: The unqualified payment methods label and subscription-only exception omit material November scope. The mapped setup gives one Dashboard path without the new account ownership distinction.
source_assessments.reason: November’s supported surfaces and configuration ownership materially qualify when and where a merchant’s rule can take effect.

answers.Q1: At https://docs.stripe.com/payments/payment-method-rules, source-stripe-payment-method-rules.md documents merchant-controlled visibility by amount, country or currency. Old raw lines 8–36 and new raw lines 9–51 require dynamic payment methods and an eligible Checkout, Payment Links, Payment Element or Express Checkout Element integration. The merchant selects Customize availability and Apply Overrides on a supported method, and Stripe uses the current exchange rate to evaluate a configured threshold in another currency. November excludes cards, wallets and the Hosted Invoice Page and keeps the named subscription creation exception. In new raw lines 37–49 the platform template rules govern direct charges and connected accounts inherit them without override. For destination charges the platform’s direct payment-method settings govern. Old raw lines 44–78 and new raw lines 59–85 keep location-formatted email testing separate from live payment results.
answers.Q2: At https://docs.stripe.com/payments/payment-method-rules, source-stripe-payment-method-rules.md needs the substantive scope and account ownership additions from new raw lines 9–16, 26–33 and 37–49. Old raw lines 19–36 retain A/B testing, dynamic enablement, the named subscription scope, currency conversion and the May Customized tag. November omits the tag language without proving removal. Old raw lines 54–78 and new raw lines 69–85 keep the Checkout and Payment Links testing behavior; Node-to-cURL, screenshots, examples and changed documentation references do not change it. Keep the reciprocal route in wiki/concepts/stripe-payment-method-rules.md, qualify the cross-reference in wiki/concepts/stripe-dynamic-payment-methods.md, and refresh the existing Stripe index and company source captions.
